lyric_idea: Chorus: "And I wish I'd done this before / And I wish people liked me more." Left half: warnings that came early (the 2023 CAIS statement, the March 2023 Pause letter, Turing's 1951 lecture). Right half: AI's public favorability turning negative (Gallup, July 2026). Rejected: the Politico Sept 2026 poll (63% 'threat to humanity') is only a Wikipedia citation, Politico is blocked and the figure is not verified; Feynman 1985 has no verbatim line tied to a named event that I could confirm. Backups, both verified: UN Secretary-General Guterres, 18 Jul 2023 (deck, quote only, no image): "Its creators themselves have warned that much bigger, potentially catastrophic and existential risks lie ahead." And NBC News poll, Feb 27-Mar 3 2026 (1,000 registered voters): 26% positive and 46% negative view of AI (net -20 is arithmetic, not stated in the source).

candidates.text: “Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority…” (full sentence: “… alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war.”)
candidates.speaker_or_outlet: Statement on AI Extinction Risk, Center for AI Safety (signed by Hinton, Bengio, Altman, Hassabis, Amodei)
candidates.verified_how: Deck source: assets/research/theory/manifest.json item cais-extinction-statement (verified: true), and tools/slides_xrisk.js caisSlide already uses the sentence verbatim. The screenshot cais-statement.png exists on disk. I did not reopen the page.
candidates.why_it_fits: Deck-first pick and the most concrete early warning: the lab CEOs signed it in May 2023. The sentence is long for a 1.5-3 s read, so use the trimmed first clause with an ellipsis and keep the attribution line. Signatory line also appears in the deck's caisSlide.

candidates.text: Pause Giant AI Experiments: An Open Letter
candidates.verified_how: Page opened via WebFetch. Title is 'Pause Giant AI Experiments: An Open Letter - Future of Life Institute'. The page shows 'Published 22 March, 2023' and a signature count of 31810 at fetch time. Verbatim call: "We call on all AI labs to immediately pause for at least 6 months the training of AI systems more powerful than GPT-4." Search summaries give other dates (Mar 28, Mar 31), so the page's own date is used. Not in the deck; no local file.
candidates.why_it_fits: The March 2023 letter is the clearest 'warning that came early' in the chorus. Use the title alone, or the 'pause for at least 6 months' clause, on a single card. A screenshot of the FLI page is needed because nothing local exists.

candidates.text: “At some stage therefore we should have to expect the machines to take control…”
candidates.speaker_or_outlet: Alan M. Turing, 'Intelligent Machinery, A Heretical Theory' (1951)
candidates.verified_how: Quote Investigator page opened via WebFetch. It gives the sentence verbatim and cites Sara Turing, Alan M. Turing (1959; 2012 Centenary ed.), ch. 14, p. 132. I did not open the primary book. The venue is disputed: QI says a Manchester lecture, while a Springer article in Philosophy & Technology (search result, not opened) says a May 1951 BBC broadcast. Do not name a venue on screen.
candidates.why_it_fits: The earliest warning in the set and literally 'before' in time. Use the clause up to 'take control' with an ellipsis. The Erewhon clause is not needed on screen.

candidates.speaker_or_outlet: Gallup (2026 Bentley-Gallup Business in Society survey)
candidates.verified_how: Page opened via WebFetch: headline 'Americans Cool Toward AI', subtitle 'After two years of improving attitudes toward AI, Americans turn skeptical.', published July 28, 2026. Survey: 3,270 US adults, fieldwork May 4-11, 2026, margin of error +/-2.4 near 50%. The stat '39% say AI does more harm than good, up from 31% in 2025' comes from the fetch's extraction, so check the exact wording on the page before using it on screen.
candidates.why_it_fits: The favorability half of the chorus ('people liked me more'). The headline is short enough for a phone read. Pair it with the 39% harm stat on a second card, using the source line above.
